pr.title: Refresh ArzoieMail documentation, manual branding and CI inventory
pr.body:
Refresh the project Markdown and inherited manual for ArzoieMail, and document delivered versus remaining work. Rebrand human-facing product prose while preserving executable/service/API identifiers, database/backup names, source paths, page filenames/slugs, code examples and historical upstream attribution. Label inherited reference material and older upgrade/integration recipes explicitly.

Rewrite the current manual entry, overview, requirements, installation/upgrade, database, SQL Express/MySQL connection, security, backup, certificate, antivirus and PHP-migration guides to match the delivered project. Remove obsolete blanket claims about bundled database prerequisites, universal Blowfish obfuscation, old PHP versions and upstream manual publication. Add docs/documentation-status.md to track remaining technical review, screenshots, renderer/routes/assets, website publication and guides for unfinished Phase 1b features. Update README, roadmap, management requirements/architecture and shared agent handoff; no domain/account implementation starts in this PR.

Add the CI inventory for four installed-server backends, exact entry points, publication gates, artifacts and automated versus manual/planned coverage. Verify PR #33's 1,315-test baseline from its successful logs: 1,206 passed on Express and 1,205 on the other three, zero failures; the extra skip is the Express-only encryption test. Separate the 100 management assertions per job, fixture-based browser checks, eight SQL TLS/auth/schema/preflight checks and coverage not currently automated. Mark #33 merged. Workflow edits correct comments only; behavior is unchanged.

Validation:
- Compared all 258 manual pages’ route metadata (slug, parent, index, is_book): unchanged.
- Verified fenced/inline/HTML code tokens are preserved across 242 inherited pages; the other 16 entry/current guides were deliberately refreshed.
- Local link checks found no newly missing targets. Three existing image references remain recorded for the renderer/asset follow-up.
- git diff --check passed. Inspected current source/workflows and downloaded PR #33 logs to substantiate the inventory.
- Markdown and workflow comments only; no application behavior or identifiers changed, and no runtime tests/previews executed on the development host. This does not publish the website or validate every inherited operational recipe.
- CI pending for the updated head; prior green runs do not validate a new commit.

Pause for maintainer review after this PR; do not merge or start the next task without confirmation.

+# CI test inventory
+
+This describes the workflows and test entry points delivered through merged PR #33. Update
+this inventory and ROADMAP's baseline when coverage or test counts change. Counts below are
+a verified snapshot, not a promise that a future commit has passed.
+
+## Automated checks
+
+| Check | Coverage | Workflow |
+|---|---|---|
+| `Release x64 (windows-2025-vs2026)` | Builds the native server, tools, tests and installer; checks runtime DLL packaging. Compilation is separate from installed-server test execution. | [build.yml](../.github/workflows/build.yml) |
+| `Tests / Regression tests` | Installs the built artifact on a clean Windows runner; runs NUnit and management checks using SQL Server Compact. | [tests.yml](../.github/workflows/tests.yml) |
+| `Tests (PostgreSQL) / Regression tests` | The same installed-server suites using the runner's PostgreSQL service. | [tests.yml](../.github/workflows/tests.yml) |
+| `Tests (MySQL) / Regression tests` | The same suites using an isolated MySQL service/data directory. | [tests.yml](../.github/workflows/tests.yml) |
+| `Tests (SQL Server Express) / Regression tests` | SQL Server 2025 Express with OLE DB 19 and verified TLS; SQL-specific checks followed by NUnit and management checks. | [tests.yml](../.github/workflows/tests.yml) |
+| `gcc`, `clang` | Build the portable core on Linux with address/undefined-behaviour sanitizers and run its CTest suite. They do not build or exercise the Windows service. | [portable-core.yml](../.github/workflows/portable-core.yml) |
+| `actionlint and zizmor` | Workflow syntax/context validation and static workflow security checks. Runs when workflow files change, or by manual dispatch. | [lint-workflows.yml](../.github/workflows/lint-workflows.yml) |
+
+Push-triggered workflows cover `master`, `feature/**`, `bugfix/**`, `techdebt/**`, `claude/**`
+and matching version branches. Build and portable-core workflows also support manual dispatch.
+Fork PR creation alone does not trigger the build; the build workflow deliberately runs on
+repository pushes. Documentation-only changes on an eligible branch still trigger normal CI.
+
+`Publish the installer` waits for the release build and **all four database jobs**, then attests
+and uploads installer/symbol artifacts. It is an artifact-publication gate, not another test suite
+or a public GitHub release. The manually dispatched [release workflow](../.github/workflows/release.yml)
+creates a draft release from an already built/tested artifact for maintainer review.
+
+Publication dependencies and branch-protection required checks are different settings. The
+workflow enforces the former; confirm the live repository rules before describing the latter.
+Green CI never authorizes an agent to merge or start the next task without the maintainer's gate.
+
+## Installed-server regression suite
+
+The four database jobs run `RegressionTests.dll` through the restored NUnit console runner
+against the installed mail service. Coverage includes SMTP, IMAP, POP3, legacy management API,
+business/persistence behavior, bound SQL values, authentication, TLS, spam/antivirus integrations,
+secret storage, backup/restore and binary hardening. Some tests depend on external services or
+explicit opt-in; a passing job does not mean every optional test ran.
+
+The native class suite is invoked from NUnit, including SQL connection-policy validation.
+`API/SqlServer.cs` additionally verifies encryption of native mail-service SQL sessions in the
+Express fixture. That database-specific test is explicitly skipped on the other three backends.
+

-This page describes how to upgrade to hMailServer latest version. If you follow these steps, the server downtime will only be a few minutes. +## Upgrade to ArzoieMail
+
+ArzoieMail preserves compatibility identifiers so an existing hMailServer installation can be
+upgraded in place. This does not guarantee that an arbitrary historical release can skip every
+intermediate migration. Use the supported source/target schema path and test the upgrade in an
+isolated VM before changing production.
+
+1. Back up the database, mail files, configuration, certificates and scripts; export the
+   installation secret key with a passphrase. Verify restoration on a separate machine/VM.
+2. Review the current system requirements and release notes. Close administration tools.
+3. For full SQL Server, prepare SQL Server 2019+, x64 OLE DB 19, its x86/x64 VC prerequisites,
+   TCP and trusted certificate configuration before installing the new mail-service binary.
+   Remove legacy provider overrides as described in the SQL Server guide. Compact is separate.
+4. Run the ArzoieMail installer and complete database setup/updating. Existing paths and database
+   settings are retained where supported. If a required SQL prerequisite is missing, setup must
+   refuse before stopping the running service or replacing files.
+5. Verify startup, schema version, credentials, queued delivery, client protocols, TLS and
+   backups. Preserve the pre-upgrade backup until the migration has been accepted.
+
+The executable, service identifier, COM ProgID, database table prefix and backup XML filename
+retain their compatibility names. Do not rename these files or keys by hand during upgrade.
+A schema upgrade is not undone by replacing only the executable; restore the complete compatible
+backup for a rollback. Older version-specific pages in this section are historical references.
+
+See [SQL Server deployment](https://github.com/jassifx/ArzoieMail/blob/master/docs/sql-server.md),

+## Supported database paths
+
+ArzoieMail has four database backends: SQL Server Compact, full SQL Server (including Express),
+MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL. These store server configuration and message metadata; message
+bodies remain in the mail data directory. Back up both components consistently.
+
+- **SQL Server Compact 4.0** is the current built-in database. It is distinct from Express and
+  remains covered by CI. SQLite replacement and automatic migration are planned, not implemented.
+- **SQL Server** uses Microsoft OLE DB 19 over TCP with required TLS and certificate validation.
+  The engine baseline is SQL Server 2019+. SQL Server 2025 Express has passed the current full CI
+  suite; that does not validate every other SQL version or high-load deployment.
+- **MySQL/MariaDB** use the bundled MariaDB Connector/C (`libmariadb.dll`). MySQL CI covers the
+  native driver's persistence path. Version-specific upgrades still need their own validation.
+- **PostgreSQL** uses the bundled libpq driver and has its own installed-server CI job.
+
+The external SQL Server driver and its prerequisites must be installed separately. See
+[SQL Server / Express deployment](https://github.com/jassifx/ArzoieMail/blob/master/docs/sql-server.md)
+for endpoint/authentication settings, trusted certificates, driver migration and offline preparation.
+The legacy description that every database option works without any extra prerequisites is obsolete.
+
+## Selection and operations
+
+Choose a backend based on the required capacity, administration skills, backup/recovery plan and
+measured workload. Express has edition/version limits; a successful functional suite is not a
+capacity guarantee. Check the relevant vendor's current limits and terms for the exact version.
+The original manual's blanket commercial-use claims about Compact are not a substitute for those terms.
+
+Use Database Setup to create/select the database. The service must have access under its actual
+Windows or SQL identity; the web panel must not receive database credentials. Preserve protected
+credentials, the installation's exportable secret key and a tested restore path when moving hosts.
+See [backup and restore](?page=backup_restore) and the current CI inventory.

-## Other Software
-
-### Database server
-
-hMailServer was designed to provide, in one single download, everything you need to run an email server. hMailServer has its own integrated database server, a light-weight version of the MSSQL database server. Should you not wish to use it, you can [select one](?page=choosing_database_engine) of the following database engines:
-
-- MySQL 4 and MySQL 5 (or MariaDB)
-- Microsoft SQL Server 2000, 2005, 2008, 2012 and 2016 (including Express, Standard and Enterprise edition)
-- PostgreSQL 8
-
-The client libraries needed to connect to these database engines are included in the hMailServer installation. For MySQL and MariaDB, hMailServer installs MariaDB Connector/C (libmariadb.dll), which connects to both. For PostgreSQL, it installs libpq from PostgreSQL 18. No client library has to be downloaded or copied manually.
-
-Notice that hMailServer is only tested with production releases of database engines. If you install an alpha or beta of for example MySQL, you should not expect hMailServer to work with it. The bundled Microsoft SQL Server Compact Edition (MS SQL CE) is not supported by Microsoft for Windows 8, Windows 8.1, Windows 10, Server 2012 or Server 2016. You will need to use an external database with these Operating Systems.
-
-### SquirrelMail
-
-If you plan to use the hMailServer password changer plugin or auto-reply plug-in with SquirrelMail, you will need SquirrelMail 1.4.7 or later.
-
-### Web administration
-
-If you plan to use PHPWebAdmin to manage your hMailServer installation via a web browser, you need to run a web server where support for PHP is available.
-
-### Incompatible software
-
-hMailServer is incompatible with the following sotware:
-
-- NetLimiter from Locktime Software. NetLimiter has an incorrectly written Windows LSP ("Winsock driver") which causes problems for hMailServer. NetLimiter works incorrectly with other software as well (including software from Microsoft) so it should never be installed on the same computer as hMailServer). The hMailServer Team has tried to get an explanation from Locktime Software about this but has not received any.
-- NOD32/IMON from ESET. hMailServer is not compatible with the IMON component in NOD32. During installation of NOD32, a warning is shown that the IMON component should not be installed on servers since it's known to cause issues with server software. (hMailServer has no problems coexisting and using NOD32 as long as the IMON component is not enabled)
-
-### Virus scanners
-
-For hMailServer to work properly, automatic virus scanning of the hMailServer Data directory must be disabled. You should configure your virus scanner to exclude the hMailServer Data directory from scanning. If you do this, it is recommended that you configure hMailServer to launch your virus scanner whenever a new e-mail is received.
-
-## Hardware
-
-### Performance
-
-The hardware requirements are very much dependent on the number of users. They also depend on whether or not you will be using IMAP support, virus scanning, filters, etc. POP3 uses much less CPU resources than IMAP, so, if you have a lot of users, POP3 is recommended. hMailServer normally uses less than 100MB of memory. The largest hMailServer installations have over 20 000 user accounts hosted on a single server.
-
-### Screen resolution
-
-The administration program for hMailServer, hMailServer Administrator, requires a screen resolution of 800x600 or above.
-
-## Technical knowledge
-
-To be able to successfully set up an email server, you need to know the basics about certain techniques related to Internet and email. You need to have a basic understanding of the following items to be able to successfully set up an email server on Windows.
-
-- Microsoft Windows
-- Domain names and host names
-- Firewalls and routers
-- DNS, Domain Name System
-- TCP/IP ports
-
-As well as knowledge on networks, and email systems you should also have knowledge on SQL database management (of your choice) if choosing an external database.
+## Platform and runtime
+
+ArzoieMail targets **64-bit Windows 10 / Windows Server 2016 or newer**. The current installer
+and imported native libraries require that baseline; historical hMailServer support for XP,
+Windows 7 or older Server releases does not apply. See BUILDING.md for the exact toolchain.
+
+Desktop administration tools use .NET 10; the installer includes the Desktop Runtime for offline
+installation when needed. The replacement web panel uses ASP.NET Core/.NET 10 and requires its
+own hosting/runtime provisioning. IIS and standalone hosting are deployment options under design;
+the panel is not yet provisioned as the production replacement by the installer.
+
+## Database
+
+| Backend | Current project status |
+|---|---|
+| SQL Server Compact 4.0 | Existing built-in backend; CI-covered. Replacement by SQLite is planned. |
+| SQL Server 2019 or newer, including Express | OLE DB 19, TCP and required TLS/certificate validation. SQL Server 2025 Express is the verified VM/CI target. |
+| MySQL / MariaDB | External backend through bundled MariaDB Connector/C; MySQL has an installed-server CI job. Validate the chosen server version. |
+| PostgreSQL | External backend through bundled libpq; installed-server CI coverage. Validate the chosen server version. |
+
+SQL Server's optional OLE DB 19 driver is not bundled: install its x64 driver and both x86/x64
+Visual C++ prerequisites, and configure trusted SQL TLS before upgrading an MSSQL installation.
+See [SQL Server deployment](https://github.com/jassifx/ArzoieMail/blob/master/docs/sql-server.md)
+and [database choices](?page=choosing_database_engine). Do not follow old SQL Server 2000 or
+bundled-MySQL instructions for a new ArzoieMail deployment.
+
+## Administration and security
+
+The desktop Administrator remains available. The new web panel/API does not use COM or direct SQL;
+the legacy COM API remains for desktop tools, setup and existing scripts. PHP is required only
+by the legacy PHP panel during migration, not by the replacement.
+
+Provide appropriate DNS, firewall/router configuration and certificates for the hostnames clients
+use. The mail-service TLS bindings and IIS web HTTPS binding are separate. Optional antivirus
+integrations require their own validated engine configuration. Defender integration is planned,
+not delivered; do not infer email scanning from the presence of Windows Defender alone.
+
+## Capacity and verification
+
+Choose CPU, RAM and storage from measured accounts, message sizes, protocol concurrency, database
+work and scanning load. This project does not publish a validated universal message-rate limit.
+The planned Defender 10,000-message pressure test is an acceptance requirement, not a benchmark
+already passed. Review [CI coverage](https://github.com/jassifx/ArzoieMail/blob/master/docs/ci-test-inventory.md)
+and [security](?page=security) before deployment.

-The hMailServer COM API throws exception in the following cases:
+The ArzoieMail COM API throws exception in the following cases:

 ## Overview
 
 hMailServer 4.2 and later supports the IMAP sort extension. This extension can improve performance when loading mailboxes that contains a large number of emails. If the IMAP client uses the IMAP sort extension, the sorting of messages are done on the server, instead of in the client. +
+ArzoieMail's Windows service identifier remains `hMailServer`; its display name is ArzoieMail.

+legacy/fallback configurations must be reviewed independently. The native executable remains

+for writable state. Upgrades may retain `ProgramData\hMailServer` or an administrator-configured
+location. Check the installed `hMailServer.ini` rather than assuming every deployment uses a default.

+protected by machine-scope DPAPI. Administrator authentication is separate. The former statement

+do not assume a backup contains portable plaintext credentials. Keep recovery passphrases and

Keep README, roadmap and shared agent memory aligned.
